title: LFP 1D: presented stimulus identity decodes strongly; omitted identity does not

claims.statement: Per-channel low-frequency (<100Hz) LFP power decodes the identity of a PRESENTED stimulus well above chance, with a clean occipital>frontal gradient. Storyline item (1), LFP arm.
claims.receipt: outputs/classification/lfp1d_stim_by_area.csv, 21 sessions, 177 cells, 5-fold CV + 100-shuffle permutation null. V2 0.790 (15/15 cells sig), V1 0.786 (21/21), V3 0.781 (12/12), V4 0.729 (21/21), TEO 0.612 (73% sig), PFC 0.557 (51%), FEF 0.537 (47%). Chance 0.5. 130/177 cells p<0.05. Run 2026-08-07, 2458.4s.

claims.statement: The same 1D LFP feature does NOT decode the identity of an OMITTED stimulus: chronological-split accuracy sits at chance in every area, with no gradient. Storyline item (2), LFP arm.
claims.receipt: outputs/classification/lfp1d_omission_by_area.csv, 21 sessions, 59 cells. Chronological half-split mean 0.484 (V3 0.513 best, FEF 0.469 worst; chance 0.5) -- the best area is 1.3 points above chance and the mean is BELOW it. Random half-split mean 0.515, again above chronological, the same persistent split-scheme gap seen in every spike analysis on this corpus.

claims.statement: The chronological split's X|R null stratum shows a strong, direction-dependent bias that cancels on averaging, which is the expected signature of slow within-session drift rather than of identity coding.
claims.receipt: Same file: R fraction predicted 'B' is 0.321 when trained on the first half and 0.702 when trained on the second half (expected 0.5 each), while the random split gives 0.499. A classifier trained early calls R trials 'A'; trained late it calls them 'B'.
claims.note: Observation of a signature. Attributing it to drift specifically is an inference, not a measurement -- no drift model has been fitted.

falsifier: Item (1) closed: a positive control that decodes at 0.79 with 100% of occipital cells significant. Item (2) closed for the 1D LFP feature specifically -- it does not extend to 2D or to any other feature.
